properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-09-14. **Revised the same day after the reference was read** — see fact:storyflows-extraction-read-and-the-two-pass-analogy-holds-in-the-order-not-in-the-definitions.

═══ THE IDEA, in his words ═══

"In the storyflow project (you can ssh to the other machine and look for the 2 pass extraction process), but this would maybe be similar in that you would have a schema (with all the SE terms defined up-front) that tell the agent how to parse a user provided description. It could be done at /genesis or /adopt, but might be good when the agent is looking is given any design related prompt to help it extract the content in a systematic extraction manner."

═══ WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING PROPOSED ═══

Not new vocabulary — a new ORDER OF OPERATIONS. Today extraction is one pass: the agent reads the user's words and produces nodes, its own judgement doing the routing in flight. The claim is that a parse against a stated structure is more systematic and more REVIEWABLE than a parse against an agent's priors. `describe_schema` already serves the vocabulary on demand; what is proposed is that it be CONSULTED AS A STEP rather than available as a lookup — the same distinction dec:idea-does-the-black-box-frame-reach-the-agent-at-call-time drew.

═══ ⭐ WHAT THE REFERENCE TURNED OUT TO BE (read 2026-09-14, code and lessons doc, on ajs77) ═══

storyflow's extraction is a three-phase fan-out of 17 focused passes that replaced one ~5,100-word monolithic prompt. The analogy HOLDS in two places and FAILS in the one place the sentence above put it:

HOLDS — ORDER. Entities first, from prose alone; then a cheap gate; then edges conditioned on the rosters the entity passes produced ("CHARACTERS PRESENT: …"). The monolith was blind to whole edge families (hierarchy 0/10 → 10/10 per-axis; relationships 40% → 100%). reflow2's capture-intent is a monolith of exactly that shape, and whether it is blind to a family is measurable on reflow2's own design.

HOLDS — GATING. A seven-flag T=0 classifier with ANCHOR-REQUIRED gating ("true only if you can point to a concrete in-prose instance") decides which passes run. "Bias toward recall" collapsed to constant-true. This is the answer to the question the first version of this node said nobody had answered — an agent is not asked to introspect on ambiguity; it is asked a narrow presence question that demands a pointer to evidence.

FAILS — DEFINITIONS. Their measured lesson #1: for concepts the model already has priors on, DO NOT define the terms — "per-type definitions are noise that dilutes the orthogonal list" (11 types, no definitions: 100% vs 40% with them). Lesson #2: for INVENTED terms the model has no prior on, a definition is not enough either — what works is an ~80-word VERB-TEST DISCRIMINATOR (entity ACTS → actual; entity is FELT → perceived; 0/5 → fixed). Alex's "query" is the second kind: a word the model has a strong prior on that points AWAY from the SE routing. So "a schema with all the SE terms defined up front" is the wrong shape; a verb test per SE axis — does it ACT (Capability), does it PROMISE (Requirement), is it WHERE TWO THINGS MEET (Interface), is it ORDERED (Flow) — is the shape with evidence behind it.

═══ THE SECOND QUESTION: WHEN ═══

- At `/genesis` or `/adopt` — once. ⚠️ Alex's failure was mid-project, on a word nobody had needed before.
- On every design prompt. ⚠️ Pays on every capture for the ambiguous minority — the objection already on file against option (b) of dec:idea-a-users-domain-vocabulary-has-no-route-into-se-vocabulary; and storyflow's own cost is ~17 calls per fragment.
- On a GATE — the storyflow shape: a cheap anchored presence check first, the heavier step only when it fires.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen, REVISED ═══

**(a) NOTHING.** ⚠️ It demonstrably failed for Alex, and its failure mode is a confident wrong category, not an error.

**(b) MEASURE FIRST — is reflow2's monolithic capture blind to a family?** Cheapest, no build, and it is the exact measurement that justified storyflow's split. Run capture-intent's routing over a corpus with known answers and count per-type recall. ⚠️ Needs a corpus with known answers, which reflow2 does not have; Alex's pseudo-project (already asked for) is the candidate.

**(c) A VERB-TEST DISCRIMINATOR PER SE AXIS, in the routing table, in place of definitions.** The one transferable object with a measured result behind it, and a prose change to one skill. ⚠️ Counter: storyflow's numbers are one domain, one model family; SE axes may not discriminate on verbs as cleanly as interiority did.

**(d) AN ANCHORED GATE BEFORE THE EXPENSIVE STEP** — "is there a boundary where two parts meet, that you can point to in what they said?" before an Interface capture. ⚠️ Counter: a gate is a second LLM judgement on every capture, and it is only worth it once (b) shows a family is being missed.

**(e) SCHEMA-FIRST ON EVERY PROMPT, AS ORIGINALLY STATED.** ⚠️ The reference argues against exactly this form: definitions hurt for known terms, and cost scales with passes.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

(b). Everything else is ordered by what (b) finds.
properties.name: OPEN — should extraction be TWO-PASS against an SE schema stated up front, the way storyflow parses, and does it run at genesis/adopt or on every design prompt?
properties.no_relation_note: Revision of an existing node; its relations (DEPENDS_ON dec:idea-the-interviews-answers-become-the-projects-own-se-reference, and the new finding recorded against it) already stand and are unchanged by this rewrite.
properties.rationale:
Recorded as an open question via the brainstorm discipline. Revised on the day it was written, after Anthony sent the agent to read the reference rather than reason from a sentence about it — and the reading moved the recommended first step from "read it" to "measure reflow2's own capture for a blind family", and moved the shape from "definitions" to "discriminators". The previous text's "THE REFERENCE HAS NOT BEEN READ" section is replaced rather than left standing, because a node whose prose says nobody has looked is a false instruction once somebody has.

Kept separate from the interview-reference question: that one asks what is KEPT, this asks in what ORDER the parse happens.
